title: He spent his life reading the story written in stone - fossilized plants that proved India's past stretched back hundreds of millions of years.

sources.text: Birbal Sahni Institute of Palaeosciences - About/History

caption:
He spent his life reading the story written in stone - fossilized plants that proved India's past stretched back hundreds of millions of years.

He became India's foremost palaeobotanist, studying fossilized plants to piece together the subcontinent's prehistoric past and brought a field that barely existed in India into serious scientific standing.

In 1946, Sahni established the Institute of Palaeobotany in Lucknow. Today, as the Birbal Sahni Institute of Palaeosciences, it remains an autonomous research body under India's Department of Science and Technology - still running, eight decades later.

Sahni didn't just study fossils - he built the institution that let India keep studying them, long after he was gone.
